svg.text: Ward trust boundaries — eight gates, each fail-closed
Authority flows only downward and in; each gate re-checks the caller. A boundary that cannot be crossed cleanly denies the capability — it never widens it.

g.text: TB-1 · Host ⇄ Store (approval)
✓ human review imports a revision and selects grants; the record is ed25519-signed and revision-bound
✓ re-approve bumps an epoch; the old epoch is rejected at the next authority check
✗ an unsigned or tampered record fails to load; a grant not requested by the manifest cannot be approved
✗ import does not approve; a failed approval attempt does not revoke a running revision (Stop/Disable first)
TB-2 · Store ⇄ Controller (admission)
✓ controller admits a signed record and snapshots the grants it will enforce for the run
✓ Grants.validate() checks counts, ids, and coverage against the manifest's requests (fail-closed)
✗ a corrupt/missing record is Unavailable, never a permission decision; the caller is not told to widen the grant
✗ a later grants.json edit cannot widen a running plugin — the admitted snapshot governs
TB-3 · Controller ⇄ Supervisor (spawn)
✓ controller verifies cgroup limits, then hands the worker controller-owned bind-fd descriptors only
✓ 512 MiB · 128 tasks · 50 % CPU · --timeout; cgroup.kill on Drop; guard() is async-signal-safe
✗ a worker RPC cannot select a limit, an executable, or an identity — all are controller-owned
✗ no --ro-bind of host paths; a grant without its prepared directory is an error, not a tmpfs downgrade
TB-4 · Supervisor ⇄ Worker (bwrap sandbox)
✓ --unshare-all · --unshare-user · --unshare-cgroup · --disable-userns · --cap-drop ALL · --clearenv
✓ restrict_bootstrap(): close_range(3..MAX) first, then re-open granted sockets O_PATH|O_NOFOLLOW, then Landlock
✓ Landlock allows only RESOLVE_UNIX on the granted sockets; /tmp, /run/plugin are tmpfs; /home is tmpfs or storage bind
✗ a connected inherited socket bypasses path-Landlock — so all fds are closed before re-opening
✗ no file→IPC grant: the worker can open a path but cannot reach a host socket through it
TB-5 · Worker ⇄ Broker (requests)
✓ authenticate_member: SO_PEERCRED uid == host uid AND the peer is in the controller's cgroup
✓ per-kind token Budget; 15 bounded delivery slots; a failed auth is still charged to the admission window
✓ with_request re-checks live authority under the store lock immediately before the host effect runs
✗ an unauthenticated peer is dropped, not queued; a revoked record aborts the whole loop
✗ a capability whose socket is absent (not admitted) cannot be connected at all
TB-6 · Worker ⇄ Compositor (input projection)
✓ the host projects key/pointer/scroll into a private Smithay display; only the focused host item receives it
✓ the keymap is built incrementally from host-delivered keys (≤ 760), never the full host keymap
✓ a layer can gain OnDemand focus only after a real click; the host arms exclusive focus for a summoned panel
✗ the worker cannot request focus, grab, or key events — only the trusted host may arm them
TB-7 · Worker ⇄ Media proxy (MPRIS)
✓ xdg-dbus-proxy is started in the controller's service and dies with it; the worker only sees a unix socket
✓ a fixed allow-list: transport/Properties/Introspect + Next/Previous/Pause/Play/Seek/SetPosition
✗ no --talk, no --own, no wildcards; OpenUri/Raise/Quit/Properties.Set are denied
✗ only one selected player name; a name mismatch is an error; the bus address must be a pathname Unix bus
TB-8 · Worker ⇄ Host (exec / http / settings / notify)
✓ exec: positive-only argv Tree, whole-argument regex \A…\z, exact executable digest, sealed copy, cgroup child
✓ http: origin+method+path+query+body scoped; AddressPolicy pins the resolved IP (anti DNS-rebinding)
✓ settings: exact own-entry keys, read/write independent, host-structure keys (id/sandbox/__proto__) rejected
✗ a host command retains full CLI authority — argv matching is not semantic safety; the reviewer's choice is the boundary
✗ notify escapes body and rejects control/RTL chars; open-url accepts only bounded http(s) with a non-empty host

svg.text: Revocation is the common thread: every gate re-reads the live store. A revoked record aborts the loop, and cgroup.kill on Drop bounds cleanup by the kernel's "populated 0" event — never a guessed retry.

A documented, intentional limitation: the approving account is the same session account (not an independent human boundary), and a completed host effect (a file written, a package installed) cannot be undone by revocation.
